sentences.text: 1. This criminal appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction dated 17.01.2022 and order on sentence dated 18.01.2022 passed in Spl. Case No.13/2021 by the Additional District and Sessions Judge - FTSC - I, UK, Karwar District (Special Court for Trial of Cases under POCSO Act).

sentences.text: 2. The rank of the parties, henceforth, will be referred to as per their rankings in the Trial Court, for convenience.

Brief facts of the case:
3. It is the case of the prosecution that on 16.12.2020, the complainant stated to have gone to the land bearing Sy.No.9 which belongs to P.W.3 - Ramakrishna for the purpose of planting areca nut seeds along with the victim girl, who is his daughter, aged about 16 years.
4.
It is further stated in the complaint that the accused had also gone to the said work along with the complainant.
On the same day, in the afternoon, during lunch break, the NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 complainant was preparing food and told the accused to bring some vegetables.
The accused took the victim girl who was minor and also mentally retarded.
The accused did not return even after a long period.
The complainant went to see the accused and he found that the accused was committing sexual assault with the victim.

5. The accused after noticing the arrival of the complainant, stood up by arranging the dress properly and requested the complainant that he should not disclose the said fact to anybody and also stated to have asked to pardon him.
However, the complainant after discussing the said fact with the relatives, lodged a complaint on 17.12.2020 around 04.35 p.m.

The jurisdictional police after having registered a case in Crime No.219/2020 for the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') along with Sections 4, 6, 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO Act') and after conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
6. To prove the case of the prosecution, the prosecution examined 19 witnesses as PWs.1 to 19 and also got NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 marked 40 documents as Exs.P1 to P40.

sentences.text: The Trial Court after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record recorded the conviction of the accused for the offence under Section 6 of POCSO Act and under Section 376 of IPC.

Being aggrieved by the Shri Chandrashekhar Pandu Siddi vs State Of Karnataka on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143631469/
2 judgment of conviction, the appellant has approached this Court seeking relief to set aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court.

sentences.text:
7. Heard Smt.Chetana S.Biraj, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri.Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State and Sri.N.G.Rasalkar, learned counsel for P.W.1.
8.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant / accused that the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court is contrary to the evidence and law and therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.

9. It is further submitted that the Trial Court failed to consider the evidence of PW.8 who had clearly deposed that, as per the report which is marked as Ex.P16, there NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 are no injuries on the body of the victim and further, no injuries are found on the private parts of the victim.
10. It is further submitted that the Trial Court ought not to have acted upon the evidence of interested witnesses.

It is also stated in the complaint and evidence of the complainant that both the complainant and accused were working in the land which belongs to CW.5 and thereafter, in the afternoon, it is alleged that the accused had committed sexual assault on the minor girl.
A complaint came to be registered on the following day around 04.35 p.m.
The delay in lodging the complaint which is fatal to the case of the prosecution if it is not explained properly.
However, the Trial Court has not discussed the delay properly and recorded the conviction which is not proper.
11. It is further submitted that when the medical evidence has not supported the incident of rape, the oral evidence of the interested witnesses loses its significance.
Such being the fact, the Trial Court should have insisted on corroboration.

Though the evidence of P.W.3 supported the case of the prosecution, the fact remains that he was the owner of the property and he has not brought to the NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 notice of other villagers at the earliest.
Therefore, the evidence of P.W.3 appears to be unbelievable and not acceptable.
In the absence of medical evidence regarding the alleged rape, the conviction ought not to have been recorded against the accused.
Therefore, the judgment of conviction is liable to be set aside.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the appellant / accused prays to allow the appeal.

12. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent vehemently justified the judgment of conviction passed by the Trial Court and further, he submitted that the findings of the Trial Court in recording the conviction appear to be proper and appropriate.
The evidence of PWs.1 and 2 who are the parents of the victim are consistent in their evidence regarding the age of the victim.
According to them, the victim was aged about 16 years as on the date of the incident.

13. It is further submitted that P.W.13 who was working as Head Mistress of Government Higher Primary School, Nandolli had deposed that after having received the requisition by the Investigating Officer, she gave the NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 school records relating to the age of the victim.
The said documents are marked as Exs.P25 and P26.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that P.W.7 who was working as Assistant Professor, Department of Forensic Medicine, Karwar had stated about the examination conducted relating to the determination of age of the victim girl and produced documents marked as Exs.P13 and P14.
As per the said report, the age of the victim girl is above 16 years and below 18 years.
15. It is further submitted that the owner of the land where both the accused and complainant were working has been examined as P.W.3.
He deposed in his evidence that around 12.00 noon, he heard a loud quarrel which was taken place between the accused and P.W.1.
He went near the place of the incident and saw that the accused was pleading to forgive him and the complainant was scolding him.
On enquiry, he learnt that the accused had committed sexual assault against the minor who was mentally retarded.
The evidence of P.W.3 supported the case of the prosecution in spite of having been subjected to cross-examination.

He being an independent witness, NC:
2024:KHC-D:14877 his evidence is reliable and trustworthy.
Therefore, there is no reason to discard his evidence.
16. It is further submitted that, P.W.8 who was working as Lady Medical Officer at Yellapur Government Hospital received a requisition from the Investigating Officer to examine the victim girl.

Though the said Doctor tried to make an enquiry of the victim girl relating to the incident, the victim was unable to talk and respond, therefore, she received information from the mother of the victim girl.

After having received the information, she examined the victim girl and submitted the report as per Ex.P16.
17.

It is further submitted that P.W.9 who was working as Associate Professor, Department of Psychiatry at KIMS Karwar stated to have conducted a test regarding the mental capacity of the victim girl and submitted the report as per Ex.P21.
As per the said report, it appears that the victim was suffering from mental illness.

18. It is further submitted that the Trial Court after appreciating the evidence of these witnesses and also appreciating the documentary evidence available on record, opined that the accused had committed offences NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 as stated supra.
Therefore, the findings of the Trial Court in convicting the accused are reasonable and appropriate and interference with the said findings may not be proper.
Hence, the appeal may be dismissed.
Making such submissions, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the appeal.

19. Sri N.G.Rasalkar, learned counsel for the complainant vehemently justified the judgment of conviction passed by the Trial Court and also adopted the arguments adopted the learned High Court Government Pleader.
He further submitted that the prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt that the appellant has committed the offence as stated in the case.

Therefore,
interference may not be necessary on the facts and circumstances of the case.
Making such submissions, learned counsel for the complainant prays to dismiss the appeal.

20. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the findings of the Trial Court in recording the conviction, this Court being an Appellate Shri Chandrashekhar Pandu Siddi vs State Of Karnataka on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143631469/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 Court, in order to reassess and re-appreciate the evidence on record, it is necessary to record the evidence of all the witnesses in brief.

sentences.text: 21. P.W.1 is the father of the victim.
According to him, he and his wife and two others along with the victim had been to work in the land of P.W.3.
He further deposed that he used to take the victim girl along with him as she was unable to maintain herself.
Further, he deposed that the accused who went to bring vegetables from the nearby garden along with the victim, however, he did not return within time.
As he was preparing the food and wanted to put the vegetables to prepare the food, he went on searching the accused and the victim.
However, he was surprised and shocked to see that the accused was committing sexual assault on the victim girl.
Though the accused pleaded him to forgive him, he discussed the matter with the elders and lodged a complaint after subjecting the victim for medical examination.

22. P.W.2 who is the wife of P.W.1 and the mother of the victim has deposed in her evidence that she was informed - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 regarding the incident of rape committed to the victim by the accused on 16.12.2020 around 2 'O' clock.
However, it is to be noted that she was at her home when the said fact was informed to her.
23. P.W.3 is the owner of the property where both the accused and complainant were working together.
He deposed that the accused was touching the feet of the complainant and requesting him that he should not disclose the fact of rape committed to the victim to anybody.
He supported the case of prosecution and nothing has been elicited to discredit his evidence.
24. P.W.6 was also working in the field of P.W.3 as one of the employees.
He deposed that till 12.30 p.m., all four persons were working in the said field and thereafter he and C.W.7 went to the neighbouring land on some work and returned around 1.00 p.m.
He further deposed that he saw that the accused was in the house of P.W.3 on the said timings.
Initially, he was not aware of the incident, however, he learnt about the incident on the following - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 day.

He further deposed that he had not made any statement before the police as per Ex.P12.
25.
P.W.7 was working as an Assistant Professor at the Department of Forensic Medicine, Karwar.
He stated to have conducted the examination of the victim girl to determine her age.
After conducting the examination, he submitted the report as per Ex.P13 and P14.
As per Ex.P13, he opined that the age of the victim girl was above 16 years and below 18 years.

sentences.text: P.W.8 was working as a Lady Medical Officer at Yellapur Government Hospital said to have conducted medical examination of the victim girl relating to the alleged offences.
She submitted her reports as per Exs.P16, P17, P18 and P19.
After she conducted the physical examination, she found no external injuries on the victim girl and thereafter, she conducted the local examination on 17.12.2020 on the victim girl.
On examination, she found that the hymen of the victim was torn and it was healed.
A question was put to her in the cross- examination that if such hymen was torn, how long it - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 would take for healing?

She deposed that the healing process commenced a week ago and further, she deposed that there were no fresh injuries on urethral meatus and vestibule, labia majora and labia minora and fourchette and introitus.
The hymen even though appears to be torn, it was healed.
27. On considering the evidence of material witnesses, namely, P.Ws.1, 2, 3, 6, it can be gathered from their evidence that the victim was a minor girl and she was mentally retarded.

The evidence relating to the mental retardation has been corroborated by the evidence of P.W.9 who conducted the mental ability test and submitted the report as per Ex.P21.
28.
The evidence of P.W.1 was contrary to the evidence of P.W.8.
According to the prosecution, the incident of rape had taken place on 16.12.2020 and P.W.1 stated in his evidence that he has seen the incident of rape which was being committed by the accused.
The victim was subjected to medical examination on the following day.

sentences.text: According to P.W.8 and as per opinion, there was no forceful recent penetration.
Such being the fact, the evidence of P.W.1 appears to be not relevant and - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:14877 unbelievable.
When the evidence of P.W.1 is not believable, the evidence of P.W.3 loses its significance.
Moreover, in this case, the prosecution has not conducted examination of the victim by making necessary arrangements like securing the presence of an interpreter in the Court etc.
Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that the findings of the Trial Court in recording the conviction appear to be erroneous and not proper.
Therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.

30. In the light of the observation made above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Appeal is allowed.
ii) The judgment of conviction dated 17.01.2022 and order of sentence dated 18.01.2022 passed in Spl.Case No.13/2021 by the Additional District and Sessions Judge - FTSC - I, UK, Karwar District (Special Court for Trial of Cases under POCSO Act) is set aside.
